entities.summary: Nuño Sánchez was a nobleman and statesman in the Crown of Aragon, born in 1190 in Zaragoza, Aragon, Spain, and died in 1247. He played a crucial role in the governance of the Crown, serving as a member of the Cortes of Aragon and participating in the kingdom's diplomacy. Nuño Sánchez was also involved in the development of the kingdom's legal system, contributing to the creation of the Laws of Aragon. His influence can be seen in the subsequent reign of his successor, King James I of Aragon. The Nuño Sánchez's legacy can be seen in the modern-day region of Aragon, where he is remembered as a key figure in the kingdom's history. The city of Zaragoza, where he was born, is home to the Casa de la Panadería, a 14th-century building that once served as his residence. The town of Sos del Rey Católico, where he died, is also named after him. Nuño Sánchez's contributions to the Crown of Aragon had a lasting impact on the region's politics, law, and culture. He is considered one of the most important figures in Aragon's medieval history.

entities.summary: Nuño Sánchez was a member of the royal court of Castile, serving as a trusted advisor to King Alfonso IX of León and later as the ruler of the County of Huelva. He played a key role in the Reconquista, a period of Christian reconquest of the Iberian Peninsula from Muslim rule. Nuño Sánchez was also a prominent figure in the politics of the Crown of Aragon, working closely with King James II of Aragon and King John of England to strengthen ties between the kingdoms. His diplomatic efforts helped to secure trade agreements and alliances between the kingdoms, paving the way for a period of relative peace in the region. As a nobleman and statesman, Nuño Sánchez left a lasting legacy in the medieval world, shaping the course of history in the Iberian Peninsula and beyond.
